# AC Frozen Coil? What Causes It and What to Do

An AC frozen coil almost always points to one of two problems. Either too little air moves across the coil, or the system has lost some of its refrigerant. Turn the cooling off, switch the fan to on and let the ice melt before you try anything else.

## Why an air conditioner coil freezes

The indoor coil runs cold on purpose. Warm air from the house passes over it, gives up its heat and keeps the metal just above freezing. Remove that steady flow of warm air and the coil temperature drops below 32 degrees. Moisture in the air then freezes onto the fins, and every new layer of ice blocks even more airflow.

A dirty filter causes most of the frozen coils our technicians find. A clogged filter starves the coil of air, and so do closed supply vents or a failing blower motor. Check the filter before anything else, because a new one costs a few dollars and takes about a minute to replace.

Low refrigerant explains most of the remaining cases. A leak lowers the pressure inside the coil, and lower pressure means a colder coil. Only a licensed technician can locate and repair that kind of leak. Systems installed before 2010 usually run on R22, and manufacturers stopped producing R22 in 2020, so every recharge costs more than the last one. Our article on [how long an AC lasts in Texas](https://www.example-air.test/blog/how-long-does-an-ac-last-in-texas/) can help you weigh that expense against a newer system.

## How to thaw a frozen coil safely

Set the thermostat to off and the fan to on. The fan pushes room temperature air across the ice and melts it within a few hours. Place a couple of towels near the indoor unit, because the drain pan can overflow while the ice melts. Install a clean filter while you wait.

Never chip or scrape at the ice. The aluminum fins bend under light pressure, and a punctured coil turns an inexpensive repair into a major one.

## When a frozen coil needs a professional

Restart the system once all of the ice has melted. If the coil freezes again with a clean filter and open vents, the cause lies somewhere inside the equipment. That is the right moment to book an [AC repair](https://www.example-air.test/ac-repair/) visit. A technician will measure the refrigerant charge, test the blower and explain what failed before any work begins. A frozen coil sometimes follows a system that [blows warm air](https://www.example-air.test/blog/why-is-my-ac-blowing-warm-air/), so mention it if you noticed both symptoms.

Homeowners who schedule regular service rarely see this problem twice. Our [maintenance plan](https://www.example-air.test/maintenance-plan/) includes a coil inspection and a refrigerant check every spring, before the long cooling season begins.
